reference_opening.argument: This video is non-scam content because it presents an instructional walkthrough for setting up Oracle support access and submitting a Cloud service request. The screens show Oracle support navigation, a Request Access step, and a technical issue form, while the included Oracle links and free-trial link are consistent with ordinary support and cloud-service use.

citations.quote: How to Create a Service Request on Oracle Cloud
In this video we walk though: - How to setup an Oracle Support account & Cloud Support account. - How to link a support account to Oracle Cloud Account. - How to create a Service Request (SR).
Service requests can be used to get technical and non-technical cloud support for your Oracle Cloud (OCI) account.

opening.argument: The video pairs a concrete viewer action with an attractive access-oriented promise. It tells viewers how to create and connect support accounts, while also presenting an Oracle “Free trial link.” That combination can function as a low-friction acquisition funnel: register, provide account information, and follow an external link in order to obtain supposedly free cloud access. The frame showing a form requesting email, organization name, and phone number reinforces that participation requires personal details. The material therefore looks less like neutral explanation and more like a solicitation built around an easy-access offer.

citations.quote: How to setup an Oracle Support account & Cloud Support account.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The title and support language do not eliminate the solicitation. The description places a free-trial link alongside instructions to create accounts, and the screenshots show collection of identifying information. Calling this “support” describes the wrapper, but does not establish that the linked offer or registration flow is safe or beneficial.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The argument turns ordinary account setup into an unsupported claim of deception. Nothing supplied promises cash, guaranteed returns, or an unusually valuable reward; the description specifically says service requests obtain cloud support. A free trial link is not itself evidence that registration is fraudulent, and the frame shows a branded account form rather than proof of misuse.

citations.quote: Service requests can be used to get technical and non-technical cloud support for your Oracle Cloud (OCI) account.

opening.argument: Several risk signals appear together: the description directs viewers to external destinations, includes a shortened bit.ly URL, promotes a free trial, and asks them to establish accounts before proceeding. The visual sequence then instructs viewers to enter email, organization, and phone information and to request access through the support portal. Even without a stated payment, this is a low-barrier acquisition path with personal-data collection and off-platform navigation. A careful judge should treat the combination as potentially deceptive rather than assuming that corporate branding and technical terminology validate every step.

citations.quote: Oracle Support: https://support.oracle.com Oracle Cloud: https://cloud.oracle.com Oracle Free trial link: http://bit.ly/2Mfa1d6

rebuttal.rebuttal: The defense emphasizes Oracle branding and technical forms, but those are precisely the elements that can make a solicitation appear legitimate. It does not explain why a shortened external link is necessary, nor why viewers must submit organization and phone details. The ordinary appearance of the portal is not independent confirmation of the offer.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: These are not the risk signals required for a scam finding. The supplied material identifies ordinary Oracle support and cloud URLs, and the account form is consistent with setting up a service account. Most importantly, there is no promise of income, investment appreciation, withdrawal, or guaranteed reward. The cited details show an operational workflow, not deceptive returns.

citations.quote: Oracle Support: https://support.oracle.com Oracle Cloud: https://cloud.oracle.com
Service requests can be used to get technical and non-technical cloud support for your Oracle Cloud (OCI) account.

opening.argument: Although presented as education, the material actively steers viewers toward participation in Oracle's ecosystem. It gives a sequence for creating an account, linking support access, requesting a support identifier, and submitting a service request, while also publishing direct support, cloud, and free-trial links. That is actionable promotion, not merely an abstract explanation. The repeated direction to navigate, fill in information, request access, and submit a form makes the viewer a prospective registrant. Framing the funnel as a tutorial can obscure the fact that it advances an external offer and collects user information.

citations.quote: In this video we walk though: - How to setup an Oracle Support account & Cloud Support account. - How to link a support account to Oracle Cloud Account. - How to create a Service Request (SR).
Oracle Support: https://support.oracle.com Oracle Cloud: https://cloud.oracle.com Oracle Free trial link: http://bit.ly/2Mfa1d6

rebuttal.rebuttal: Instructional framing does not answer the promotional concern. The description supplies multiple direct links, including a free-trial link, and the visuals show the viewer being led through registration and submission. Explaining how to participate is itself evidence that the content is steering viewers, regardless of whether it uses the language of an advertisement.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: Steering viewers through a legitimate support workflow is not equivalent to a scam promotion. The listed steps concern support-account setup and service requests, and the frames show Oracle support interfaces and a technical issue form. The argument identifies participation but fails to show any fraudulent promise, payment demand, guaranteed reward, or concealed outcome.
